cards.explanation: The answer is Timothy, friends. Paul calls him "our brother" right there in the opening line (2 Corinthians 1:1). So this letter goes out with two names on it, not one. I've stamped a lot of cookies in my day, and I can tell you a batch goes better with a second pair of hands.

The answer is False, friends. Paul and Timothy aren't the source. The text says "Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ." (2 Corinthians 1:2). Paul is just the guy handing over the delivery slip, and he tells you exactly whose name is on the package.

The answer is so we can comfort others in trouble, friends. Paul says God "…comforts us in all our troubles, so that we can comfort those in any trouble with the comfort we ourselves have received from God." (2 Corinthians 1:4). So the comfort isn't meant to sit in a jar on your shelf. It's meant to be passed along, like a warm batch you carry next door.

The answer is comfort, friends! Paul writes, "For just as the sufferings of Christ overflow to us, so also through Christ our comfort overflows." (2 Corinthians 1:5). Notice the word is overflow, not trickle. Paul says the comfort comes through Christ, and there's plenty of it.

The answer is the Corinthians' comfort, friends! Paul writes, "If we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation; if we are comforted, it is for your comfort…" (2 Corinthians 1:6). The "your" is the Corinthians, the folks he's writing to. Whether Paul is hurting or being comforted, he's looking out for them.

The answer is salvation, friends! Paul says, "If we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation…" (2 Corinthians 1:6). Those are big words to hang on a hard season. That's the word Paul chose, and he put it right next to comfort.

The answer is True, friends. Paul says the Corinthians' comfort "…accomplishes in you patient endurance of the same sufferings we experience." (2 Corinthians 1:6). So the comfort does real work in them. It helps them hold on through the very same kind of sufferings Paul and Timothy go through.

The answer is that they share in the sufferings and will share the comfort, friends! Paul says, "…our hope for you is sure, because we know that just as you share in our sufferings, so also you will share in our comfort." (2 Corinthians 1:7). The Corinthians share in the sufferings now, and Paul says they will share in the comfort. So his hope for them stands on solid ground.

The answer is far beyond our ability to endure, friends. Paul says, "We were under a burden far beyond our ability to endure…" (2 Corinthians 1:8). That's not "a rough week." He's telling the Corinthians it was more than they could carry.

The answer is True, friends, and Paul says it plainly. Under that burden, "…we despaired even of life." (2 Corinthians 1:8). I think that's a heavy thing to admit to a church. Paul doesn't dress it up, and that honesty is a gift to anyone who's been there.

The answer is ourselves, friends! Paul says it was "…in order that we would not trust in ourselves, but in God, who raises the dead." (2 Corinthians 1:9). So the point was to move their trust off themselves and onto God. That is the reason Paul gives.

The answer is that God raises the dead, friends. Paul says they should trust "…in God, who raises the dead." (2 Corinthians 1:9). Think about where Paul was standing when he said it, under what felt like a sentence of death. Of all the things Paul could say about God there, he chose to name this.

The answer is False, friends! Paul says, "He has delivered us from such a deadly peril, and He will deliver us." (2 Corinthians 1:10). Then he keeps going: "In Him we have placed our hope that He will yet again deliver us…" After that rescue, Paul's hope is still on God to deliver again.

The answer is prayers, friends! Paul says God will deliver "…as you help us by your prayers." (2 Corinthians 1:11). So the Corinthians have a real part in this. They may be far away, but they're helping.
